title: Analysis of Choroid Thickness on OCT Image Using MATLAB
author: Chao-Yuan Yeh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.imqcc5w

steps.title: Install MATLAB and Toolbox
steps.instruction: Ensure MATLAB 2016b or newer is installed on your computer together with the Image Processing Toolbox.

steps.title: Export OCT images
steps.instruction: Using the Optovue OCT machine, export cross‑line OCT images. Acquire four cross‑line images for each eye to allow interpolation (a single cross‑line image can still be processed).

steps.title: Process raw OCT images
steps.instruction: Run the script OCT_file_processing.m. The script processes raw images generated by Optovue OCT machines, renames the files for easier handling, extracts image content from cross‑line and line scans, and saves each image as a TIFF file.

steps.title: Run image analysis script
steps.instruction: Execute OCT_ImageAnalysis_for_CrossLine.m on all TIFF files produced in the previous step.

steps.title: Draw contours and compute thickness
steps.instruction: Follow the on‑screen prompts: draw the contour of the retina on the left side of the image, then draw the contour of the choroid on the left side. After completing the left side, the program calculates choroid thickness (red auxiliary lines are perpendicular to the curve, green lines show the calculated thickness). Repeat the same drawing procedure for the right side of the image. A summary figure displaying the thickness measurements will then appear.

steps.title: Compare data across eyes
steps.instruction: After processing all four cross‑line images for both eyes, run OCT_Data_Comparison.m. The script generates interpolated data, plots choroid thickness at the eight corners, displays an interpolated picture, and creates an Excel (.xls) file summarizing the statistics.
